title: Salvianolic acid B ameliorate alopecia by simultaneously targeting Wnt/beta-catenin and mTORC2/Akt signaling.
authors: Cen, Junjie; Tang, Xin; Xu, Nan; Hong, Yiyong; Liu, Tian; Zhou, Lei; Liao, Zhikai; Wan, Miaojian
one_liner_zh: 该文研究丹参酚酸B通过Wnt/β-catenin和mTORC2/Akt信号通路治疗脱发，核心是药物作用机制，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Alopecia is a prevalent clinical condition with currently limited therapeutic options. Salvianolic acid B (Sal B) has demonstrated promising regenerative properties across various disease models. However, its potential role in the treatment of alopecia and the underlying mechanisms remain largely unexplored. OBJECTIVE: To elucidate the role and mechanisms of Sal B in hair regeneration, we evaluated its effects on hair loss model in vivo and in vitro, and integrated multi-omics analysis. METHODS: We performed reverse molecular docking screening using the LRP6 receptor (PDB: 7NAM) to identify Sal B as a top candidate. Network pharmacology and molecular docking were used to predict target genes and binding affinity. Sal B was treated with cultured DPCs and hair follicles to investigate its effects on DPC proliferation. In vivo efficacy was evaluated in murine alopecia and AGA. Integrated multi-omics analysis, complemented by Western blot and PCR, was employed to elucidate the key signaling pathways. RESULTS: Sal B bound strongly to LRP6 and promoted DPC proliferation, migration, and stemness. It enhanced hair shaft elongation in vitro and stimulated hair regeneration in mice, outperforming minoxidil in AGA models. Multi-omics analyses revealed enrichment in mTOR signaling, matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs), and MAPK pathways. Sal B activated mTORC2/Akt signaling, upregulated RICTOR, downregulated DEPTOR, and enhanced phosphorylation of Akt and GSK-3beta, leading to beta-catenin stabilization. It also increased expression of MMP9, MMP3, MMP1, and activated ERK and p38. CONCLUSION: Sal B promotes hair regeneration through dual activation of the Wnt/beta-catenin and mTORC2/Akt pathways, and upregulation of MMPs and MAPKs.
abstract_zh: 背景：脱发是一种常见的临床疾病，目前治疗选择有限。丹酚酸B（Salvianolic acid B, Sal B）已在多种疾病模型中显示出有前景的再生特性。然而，其在脱发治疗中的潜在作用及潜在机制仍 largely 未被探索。目的：为阐明Sal B在毛发再生中的作用和机制，我们评估了其在体内和体外脱发模型中的效果，并整合了多组学分析。方法：我们使用LRP6受体（PDB: 7NAM）进行反向分子对接筛选，将Sal B确定为顶级候选物。网络药理学和分子对接用于预测靶基因和结合亲和力。Sal B处理培养的毛乳头细胞（DPCs）和毛囊，以研究其对DPC增殖的影响。体内疗效在小鼠脱发和雄激素性脱发（AGA）模型中评估。整合多组学分析，辅以Western blot和PCR，用于阐明关键信号通路。结果：Sal B与LRP6强结合，促进DPC增殖、迁移和干性。它在体外增强毛干伸长，并在小鼠中刺激毛发再生，在AGA模型中优于米诺地尔。多组学分析揭示mTOR信号、基质金属蛋白酶（MMPs）和MAPK通路的富集。Sal B激活mTORC2/Akt信号，上调RICTOR，下调DEPTOR，并增强Akt和GSK-3beta的磷酸化，导致beta-catenin稳定化。它还增加MMP9、MMP3、MMP1的表达，并激活ERK和p38。结论：Sal B通过Wnt/beta-catenin和mTORC2/Akt通路的双重激活，以及MMPs和MAPKs的上调，促进毛发再生。
